name: South Carolina
summary: A white palmetto tree and a white crescent on indigo blue. The crescent comes from the 1775 Moultrie flag, and the palmetto honours the fort of palmetto logs that withstood a British attack in 1776.
origin: In 1775 Colonel William Moultrie designed a blue flag with a crescent for South Carolina troops; the blue matched their uniforms and the crescent their cap badges.
On 28 June 1776 the palmetto-log fort on Sullivan's Island withstood a British naval bombardment, as the soft wood absorbed cannonballs. The palmetto was added to the flag in 1861.

colors.name: Indigo blue
colors.meaning: The uniforms of South Carolina's Revolutionary troops; also indigo, a colonial cash crop.

symbols.name: Palmetto tree
symbols.meaning: The defence of Fort Moultrie in 1776.

symbols.name: Crescent
symbols.description: A white crescent in the upper hoist.
symbols.meaning: From the silver crescents on the soldiers' caps; sometimes interpreted as a gorget, an officer's neck armour.

facts: Palmetto Day, 28 June, commemorates the 1776 battle.
A 2023 committee proposed standardising the palmetto design, after many versions appeared on merchandise.
The flag is one of the most widely used on clothing in the US.
clues: A white palmetto tree and crescent on indigo blue.
Its tree honours a fort whose logs absorbed cannonballs.
Its crescent comes from soldiers' cap badges in 1775.
